title: Ringed open extension, scalar restriction and normalized strict limits
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be a quasi-compact open immersion of arbitrary schemes, on their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $a:R\to S$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $T$, and use the restricted rings $R_U,S_U$ on the slice site $U$ [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Write $r_V:\operatorname{Mod}(S_V)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_V)$ for scalar restriction, $V=U,T$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and $J_R,J_S$ for sheafified ringed open extension [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. The same letters denote exact termwise functors on complexes, strict inverse sequences indexed by $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$, and their unbounded derived categories [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit].
There is a canonical natural isomorphism $e:r_TJ_S\xrightarrow{\sim}J_Rr_U$, induced by the identity of the underlying extension presheaves before abelian sheafification. It identifies the units and counits of the two open-extension/restriction adjunctions, on sheaves, complexes and derived strict towers.
Countable products of these pro-etale module sheaves are exact [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Each $J_R,J_S$ has its invertible canonical product comparison, including the empty product; $r_U,r_T$ have the identity comparison on underlying abelian sheaves [lem-cbc-ringed-open-extension-products]. Write $L_{V,R},L_{V,S}$ for total right derived inverse limit and, for any of these four functors $F$, use precisely the normalized comparison $\lambda_F:FL\xrightarrow{\sim}LF^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit], with its signed Roos and K-injective resolution normalization. For every $M\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(S_U))$ one has
$$L_{T,R}(e_M)\circ\lambda_{r_T,J_SM}\circ r_T(\lambda_{J_S,M})=\lambda_{J_R,r_UM}\circ J_R(\lambda_{r_U,M})\circ e_{L_{U,S}M}.$$
The equality is natural in derived strict-tower maps. The comparisons carry the canonical maps from every strict augmentation $\Delta C\to M$ to the corresponding maps after open extension and scalar restriction. Thus they identify quotient-tower completion units whenever $M$ is a quotient tower. No flatness of $a$, boundedness of $M$, or quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $T$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use the slice-site identification of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. For an $S_U$-module sheaf $N$, the two extension presheaves have the same abelian groups and restriction maps: at $V$ they are $\bigoplus_{\varphi:V\to U}N(V,\varphi)$. Their $R(V)$-actions are both $r(s_\varphi)_\varphi=(a_V(r)s_\varphi)_\varphi$, by [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], their abelian sheafifications coincide and the induced $R$-actions coincide by uniqueness of the extending action. The identity thus induces $e_N:r_TJ_SN\to J_Rr_UN$ and its inverse. A map of $N$ acts on each summand by the same map on either side, so $e$ is natural.

For the adjunction of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], a map $h:N\to j^*Q$ extends to $J N\to Q$ by sending the generator $s$ in the summand indexed by $\varphi:V\to U$ to $h_{(V,\varphi)}(s)\in Q(V)$, then using sheafification. Conversely restrict such a map and precompose with the summand inclusion; these operations are inverse since all summand generators generate the presheaf and sheafification has unique factorization. Consequently $\eta_N$ sends $s$ to its summand generator followed by sheafification and $\epsilon_Q$ sends each generator to the same section of $Q(V)$. Scalar restriction changes none of these maps. Also $j_R^*r_T=r_Uj_S^*$ objectwise. Thus $j_R^*(e_N)\,r_U(\eta_N^S)=\eta_{r_UN}^R$ and $\epsilon_{r_TQ}^R\,e_{j_S^*Q}=r_T(\epsilon_Q^S)$, with the displayed restriction identification understood.

proof.text: Scalar restriction preserves kernels because they are sectionwise kernels with the restricted action; it preserves cokernels because sectionwise quotient groups and their abelian sheafification are unchanged, with the unique restricted action. These kernel/cokernel descriptions are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and the action is [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Hence $r_U,r_T$ are exact. Both $J$ and both $j^*$ are exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. For strict towers the same conclusions hold levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]; the natural transformations of Steps 1–2 satisfy the tower transition equations by their naturality. Apply all functors and transformations in every cochain degree. Exactness permits descent to the unbounded derived categories by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. The derived adjunction of [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction] has the localized original unit and counit, so the identities in Step 2 descend as well.

source.place: Tags 03CY, 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact); derived localization uses the specified exact-derived adjunction

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise], a product is the sectionwise product with coordinate actions. Thus restricting scalars gives exactly the same underlying product and projections, including the empty product, whose underlying group is zero. Invertibility of the canonical product comparisons for $J_R,J_S$ is [lem-cbc-ringed-open-extension-products], applicable since $j$ is quasi-compact; the base need not be quasi-compact or quasi-separated. Countable products are exact in each of the four ringed categories by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], for arbitrary ring sheaves. Together with Step 3 this verifies all hypotheses of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] for each of $r_T,J_S,J_R,r_U$. Write $\phi_F$ for their canonical product maps and $\kappa_F$ for the maps on the two signed Roos summands specified by that node.

source.place: Tag 09BP (lemma-j-shriek-limits); the ringed product and normalized exact-product comparison statements cited here

proof.text:
Hereafter set $A=r_TJ_S$ and $B=J_Rr_U$. For any countable family $(N_n)$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(S_U)$, with $P=\prod_nN_n$, form
$$u=(\prod_ne_{N_n})\,\phi_{r_T,(J_SN_n)}\,r_T(\phi_{J_S,(N_n)}),\qquad v=\phi_{J_R,(r_UN_n)}\,J_R(\phi_{r_U,(N_n)})\,e_P.$$
Both have domain $AP$ and codomain $\prod_nBN_n$. For every projection $\pi_n$ the defining projection equations for $\phi$ give $\pi_nu=e_{N_n}A(\pi_n)$ and $\pi_nv=B(\pi_n)e_P$. These are equal by naturality of $e$ from Step 1, so $u=v$ by the product universal property. This is a calculation with the canonical maps of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit], rather than a choice of a product isomorphism.

source.place: Final paragraph: apply the exact product-preserving functor to defining derived limits; explicit product projection calculation

proof.text:
For a strict tower complex $M$, let $H_M^q=P_M^q\oplus P_M^{q-1}$ and $d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$, as fixed in [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. Apply Step 5 separately to the families $(M_n^q)_n$ and $(M_n^{q-1})_n$. Naturality of $e$ for the two biproduct projections shows that $e_{H_M}$ is diagonal in these coordinates. Its naturality for the differentials and transitions shows that the resulting equality is an equality of chain maps, with the same minus sign on both sides. In notation
$$K_A=\kappa_{r_T,J_SM}\,r_T(\kappa_{J_S,M}),\qquad K_B=\kappa_{J_R,r_UM}\,J_R(\kappa_{r_U,M}),$$
the equality is
$$H(e_M)K_A=K_Be_{H_M}.$$
All maps are natural for strict tower chain maps. The cited normalized comparison provides their descent to the derived categories.

source.place: Final paragraph, canonical derived-limit comparison; explicit calculation on both signed Roos summands

proof.text:
Let $\theta$ denote the normalized natural isomorphism $L\to H$ of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]; its normalization agrees with K-injective resolution, not just with an unspecified Roos triangle. Substitute $\lambda_{F,M}=\theta_{FM}^{-1}\kappa_{F,M}F(\theta_M)$ in the left-hand side of the required equation. The middle factors $r_T(\theta_{J_SM})$ and its inverse cancel. Naturality of the target $\theta$ for $e_M:AM\to BM$ then makes that side
$$\theta_{BM}^{-1}H(e_M)K_A A(\theta_M).$$
Substitute the same formula on the right-hand side and cancel $J_R(\theta_{r_UM})$ with its inverse. Naturality of the derived $e$ for $\theta_M:LM\to H_M$ gives $B(\theta_M)e_{LM}=e_{H_M}A(\theta_M)$, so the right-hand side is
$$\theta_{BM}^{-1}K_Be_{H_M}A(\theta_M).$$
Step 6 proves these expressions equal. The four functor occurrences and the target limit are exactly those in the statement. Naturality of $\lambda$ and $e$ makes the resulting equality natural for every derived strict-tower morphism, including morphisms represented by roofs.

source.place: Final paragraph applying the exact-functor/derived-limit comparison; agent-written expansion of its specified normalized formula

proof.text: For a strict augmentation $\gamma:\Delta C\to M$, [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] states that $\lambda_F\,F(u_\gamma)=u_{F\gamma}$. In the signed coordinates this is the equality sending $c$ to $((F\gamma_n)(c),0)$, since $\phi_F$ is characterized by its projections. Apply this assertion successively along $J_S,r_T$ and along $r_U,J_R$. Naturality of $e$ at $\gamma_n$ identifies the resulting augmentations: $e_{M_n}A(\gamma_n)=B(\gamma_n)e_C$. Step 7 therefore identifies their canonical derived maps after either composite. A quotient-tower completion unit is the map of its strict quotient augmentation, so it is included. In particular exactness preserves the quotient maps used in such an augmentation. The argument used neither preservation of K-injectives by scalar restriction nor tensoring along $a$; no flatness or boundedness is needed.

source.place: Final paragraph applying the comparison to defining derived limits; augmentation clause of the normalized strict-limit comparison
